title: Stochastic spike capture — lab journal
content:
Quick context:
- Goal: capture and characterize intermittent ~50–200ms p99 spikes that show up under stochastic arrival patterns (not steady qps). Wanted lightweight reproducible harness to provoke and log the waveform.
- Hypothesis: spikes are correlated with (a) cold KV cache misses + prefix mismatch, (b) driver-side batching boundary alignment, or (c) occasional GC/pyalloc stalls in python shim.

Environment / harness:
- Model: redwood-v1-medium (16-bit -> quantized int8 path) on a single GPU node (g4dn.xlarge equivalent for dev, prod-equivalent runs on a2-large).
- Runtime: serving-runtime@main (commit 6b7d9e), small changes: disabled auto-batch coalescer for isolation, kernel selection logging turned on.
- Load generator: custom replay harness (replay-tiny.js) that supports poisson/clustered arrivals + k6 for steady comparisons.
- Workload: prompt length 64 tokens, output length cap 128, typical seq length 192. Mix: 90% text-gen, 10% chat-ish (function-less).
- Cache state toggles: cold (restart process + flush), partially-warm (only K/V for common prefixes warmed), warm (ran linear warmup with 2k requests). Also tested with prefix-priming table.

Experiment runs (high level):
1) Poisson-λ sweep: target mean qps 40, 80, 160. For each: 30m steady with per-request lat hist collection.
   - Observed: mean latency stable across means. p95 moves slightly with qps. p99 had intermittent spikes (single-request events) that were independent of mean qps. Spikes distribution: clusters at 120–210ms, rare >300ms.
2) Clustered arrival bursts: 5s bursts every 60s (burst peak qps ~600) with background 20 qps.
   - Observed: after burst, short tail (50–150ms) for ~15s before returning. When cache partially warm, tail shorter.
3) Prefix-mismatch test: randomize 40% of prefixes so they miss common cache entries.
   - Observed: p99 spikes concentration increased, especially if miss hits aligned with driver batch flush boundary.
4) GC shim probe: added explicit memtouch and triggered minor GC (python) in controlled runs.
   - Observed: occasional ~80–140ms spikes synchronized with GC events. But not the full explanation for the larger 200ms outliers.

Telemetry and traces:
- Traces show a repeated pattern on large spikes: request enqueued -> scheduled -> GPU-kernel-run (normal) -> wait for kv-lookup path -> cache miss -> blocking fetch (disk or remote) -> retry path -> resumed. There is a gap of ~70–180ms at the kv-lookup resolution.
- Kernel-level logs indicate no kernel recompile or expensive fallback during the events.
- Worker thread stacks (captured with lightweight pstack) show a small fraction blocked on network io in cache-fetch path.

Hypotheses refined:
- Primary: intermittent remote-KV fetch tail. The cache-miss path falls back to a remote metadata store (older code-path) that times out or is queued behind a rate limiter, producing a long stall.
- Secondary: request alignment with batching edges amplifies the impact: if a cache-miss request sits in a batch, the entire batch could be delayed by the miss resolution (amplifies p99).
- Tertiary: rare GC/alloc stalls add noise, not principal cause.

Mini root-cause evidence: 
- When we force all cache lookups to local-inmemory (bypass remote), spikes disappear in identical arrival patterns (run 2026-02-22-18).
- When we simulate the remote store being slow (sleep 100–200ms) we reproduce the p99 histogram shape almost exactly.

Quick action items (low effort first):
- Add bounding: ensure a cache-miss cannot block the GPU-serving thread for >10ms. Introduce async miss handling with placeholder/exact-fallback policy (Ishan taking sketch).
- Short term: increase cache locality by pre-priming hot prefixes for services using burst patterns. Add priming job (cron) per tenant.
- Add metrics: record cache-miss origin and lat bucket (local/remote/durable). Add request-level flag if a batch had any cache-miss.
- E2E: run a canary patch that transforms miss path into async fetch with stale-while-revalidate semantics. Monitor p99 and service-level error rates.

Notes to self / fragments:
- Could also look at driver-side batching window size: when using 8ms coalescing window, misses are less visible (they get popped out), but coalescing increases mean latency slightly. Tradeoff experiment needed.
- Ticket tie-ins: link to JIRA-3782 (KV miss amplification), follow-up PR at /serving-runtime#842 (async-miss-prototype).
- Checkpoint: put a short reproducible harness into repo under perf/replays/spike-capture to let others run locally. Keep payloads small.

Raw sample outputs (p99 summary):
- cold cache poisson 80qps: p50 42ms / p95 68ms / p99 188ms (99.9th 322ms)
- warm cache poisson 80qps: p50 36ms / p95 60ms / p99 89ms (99.9th 130ms)
- clustered burst (peak 600) background 20: p99 210ms tail for 15s after bursts

Open questions / things to test next: 
- Run full prod-equivalent nodes (a2 Large) to verify this behaves similarly at HW-level. The dev g4 proxies sometimes mask timing.
- Validate remote-KV queue/backpressure metrics (are there spikes in remote store Q depth correlated?).
- Try tiny async-miss prototype (return early cached placeholder) + reconciliation, measure quality regressions.
- Explore batching boundary nudges: jitter enqueue time slightly to de-align misses from batch flush windows. Cheap experiment.

Conclusion (current):
- Not a serving-kernel or model compute issue. Dominant signal points to KV cache miss amplification + its interaction with batching edges. Quick wins: async miss path + priming + better observability.

Scratch TODOs (ordered):
- [ ] drop lightweight harness into repo (perf/replays/spike-capture) + README (Noelle)
- [ ] spike: async-miss POC in runtime (Ishan)
- [ ] metric: per-batch-miss flag + remote-miss buckets (Mira)
- [ ] run prod-equivalent node replay and attach flamegraphs (Noelle / Mira)
- [ ] update runbook with detection pattern and mitigation steps

End of log.
